edbDesc: A naturally occurring optical phenomenon in which light rays are bent to produce a displaced image of distant objects or the sky.
title: Mirage
description: Over hot ground the air near the surface is thinner, so light skimming it bends upward and you see a shimmering 'pool' that is really the sky. Gaspard Monge explained it in 1798 while in Egypt with Napoleon's army.
effect: light bends as it passes through air of changing temperature, shifting images
usedIn: Photothermal-deflection ('mirage') spectroscopy for measuring faint absorption in coatings
Gradient-index (GRIN) lenses in endoscopes and fibre connectors
Schlieren imaging of shock waves and air flows
strength: The bending is only a fraction of a degree, but over a few hundred metres of hot road it shifts the image by metres.
pickWhy: Bending in a gradient is distinct from the deck's refraction card at a single surface, and it drives real instruments; kept.
